caption:
A PD report, written while the borrower is still talking.

A housing-finance PD visit runs about 25 minutes. Writing it up takes a median of 52 more, and 1 in 3 reports comes back to the officer. Real-Time PD changes the order of the work.

Darwix listens to the discussion in Hindi, English or Hinglish, fills the 61-field PD form live, ties every value to the sentence that produced it, keeps conflicting answers side by side for the officer to settle, and hands credit a draft that carries its own evidence.

Credit decisions stay with the credit team.

One shop. Four different monthly sales figures.

In a housing-finance case the LOS says one number, the borrower says another, and the bank, GST and supplier records say a third. Credit ends up reconciling by hand.

Evidence Intelligence reads the PD conversation as evidence, checks every fact against every source, rebuilds income, EMIs and own contribution, and raises only the findings that matter. Every value keeps its source. Every adopted value is chosen by a reviewer and recorded.

Credit decisions stay with the credit team.

A conversation should end in a record, not in someone's memory.

In most BFSI workflows the important part of an interaction is said once, remembered imperfectly and typed up later. Darwix AI works on the interaction itself. It prepares the context, listens, structures what is said, checks it against documents and systems, guides the person in the room, and keeps the audit trail.

Every value keeps its source and its state. Consequential decisions stay with a person.

caption:
Which of today's signals should a relationship manager act on?

An RM's inbox fills with notifications every week, and most of them change nothing for a client. The skill is knowing which ones do.

Alert Intelligence listens for signals, matches them to each client's holdings and limits, and scores relevance. The reason is shown with the score. The RM sees what happened, who is exposed and a conversation they can have. Contacting the client waits for supervisor approval.

caption:
A recorded Yes does not prove the customer understood the policy.

A scripted verification call confirms that a customer said yes. It does not show whether they understood the premium term, the product type or what was sold to them.

Video PIVC verifies the exact policy on the proposal. It checks identity, tests understanding, records informed consent and flags where the customer's words differ from the form. The reviewer sees the exception with its evidence, not the whole recording.

The insurer remains the issuing authority.

slides.title: A recorded Yes does not prove understanding.
slides.body: Video PIVC for life insurance.

slides.title: Same call. Two different policies.
slides.body: The customer says: The premium is for five years and the plan works like a fixed deposit. | The proposal says: A ten-year premium term on a unit-linked plan.

slides.title: Five things the call verifies
slides.body: Identity: Presence, liveness and face match where approved | Policy: The exact policy on the proposal, not a generic script | Mis-selling: Gaps between what was sold and what was understood | Consent: Informed audio-visual consent | Audit: Evidence a reviewer can inspect

slides.title: What the reviewer opens
slides.body: The field: Which proposal value was tested | The statement: What the customer actually said | The evidence: Timestamp, clip and confidence | The route: Verified, exception or re-verify

slides.title: Six possible outcomes
slides.body: Verified: Identity, policy and consent confirmed | With exception: Confirmed, with a recorded exception | Needs review: A reviewer decides | Re-PIVC: The call is repeated | Declined: The customer did not proceed | Failed: Verification did not pass

slides.title: It never forces disagreement into a false confirmation.
slides.body: If understanding differs from the proposal, the call records the gap. The insurer remains the issuing authority.
